newsitem.title: USA: San Francisco board set to rescue $1.2 bln project.
newsitem.headline: San Francisco board set to rescue $1.2 bln project.

text.p: San Francisco supervisors were expected to vote by Thursday to rescue a $1.167 billion rail extension project that failed passage this week by a narrow margin, local officials said.
The Board of Supervisors on Monday came up one vote short on a resolution critical to the proposed Bay Area Rapid Transit (BART) District extension to San Francisco International Airport.
The resolution would authorize San Francisco to deduct funds from its annual payments to BART in the event the transportation authority defaults on its rent to the airport.
Last week, San Francisco Airport Commission approved the lease agreement, allowing BART to build rail facilities at the airport for an annual rent of $2.5 million for 50 years.

Supervisor Mabel Teng, who has been traveling in Asia with a trade delegation, plans to return to San Francisco to support the BART resolution, giving it the votes it will need to pass, her office said.
The Board of Supervisors was scheduled to vote on the measure on Thursday.
The 8.7-mile, $1.167 billion project would extend BART to San Francisco International Airport.
